label: Autism diagnosis rate
source: AIHW / ABS Survey of Disability Ageing and Carers
description: Australians with an autism spectrum disorder diagnosis per 100,000 population. Has risen approximately 4-fold since 2009 — from around 75 to over 260 per 100,000.
explainer: Autism diagnosis rates have increased dramatically since 2009. This almost certainly reflects expanded diagnostic criteria (DSM-5 broadened the definition in 2013), greater public awareness, reduced stigma, improved screening, and NDIS funding incentives for formal diagnosis — rather than a genuine biological increase. The 2023 ABS Survey found 1 in 40 Australians have an autism diagnosis. Do not interpret this as evidence of an autism epidemic without understanding the diagnostic expansion context.
projection_source: AIHW projections based on current diagnostic trends and NDIS registration data.
notes: IMPORTANT: The dramatic rise primarily reflects expanded diagnostic criteria (DSM-5 2013), greater awareness, reduced stigma and NDIS funding incentives — not necessarily a biological increase in prevalence.
